competencies.name: System Design
competencies.definition: Designs services that meet stated load, failure and data constraints, and explains the trade-offs.

anchors.1: Cannot produce a workable design, or ignores the stated constraints.
anchors.2: Workable happy-path design; misses failure modes or capacity limits when prompted.
anchors.3: Sound design that handles the stated load and at least two failure modes, with trade-offs named.
anchors.4: Sound design plus quantified capacity reasoning and a migration or rollout plan, unprompted.

competencies.name: Code Quality & Testing
competencies.definition: Writes readable, tested code and refactors safely.

anchors.1: Code does not run or has no structure.
anchors.2: Runs, but untested and hard to change.
anchors.3: Readable, tested core paths, sensible names and boundaries.
anchors.4: Tests drive the design; edge cases covered; refactors with confidence.

competencies.name: Debugging & Operations
competencies.definition: Finds root causes in a running system using logs, metrics and traces.

anchors.2: Finds symptoms but not the cause.
anchors.3: Finds the root cause with a methodical narrowing approach.
anchors.4: Finds the cause, proposes a fix and a guard that prevents recurrence.

competencies.name: Communication
competencies.definition: Explains technical reasoning clearly to engineers and non-engineers.

anchors.4: Adapts the explanation to the audience and surfaces disagreement constructively.

competencies.name: Ownership
competencies.definition: Takes responsibility for outcomes beyond the assigned task.

anchors.1: No example of owning an outcome.
anchors.3: A specific example of driving an outcome end to end.
anchors.4: Several examples, including fixing something nobody assigned.

competencies.name: Collaboration
competencies.definition: Works through disagreement and helps teammates succeed.

anchors.3: A specific example of resolving a disagreement on the merits.
anchors.4: Examples of raising the team's output, e.g. mentoring or unblocking others.
